_comment: PER-FUNCTION PRESENTATION WALLS for the tactical migration domain (TACT-DOMAIN, 2026-08-24).
Consumed by tools/gen_migration.py via tools/data/migration/tact.json `select.cut_names_from`.
A listed function is REACHED by the domain and never migrated: the revised M6 exit keeps render,
UI, sound and platform in the original binary. An UNLISTED member is a MEMBER, and that default
is the safe direction -- a wrongly-kept member costs translation work and shows up in the ledger,
a wrongly-placed wall removes a subtree silently.
WHY THIS IS A NAME LIST AND NOT A PREFIX LIST. Both directions were measured on this closure and
both fail. llm_tact_active_unit_count_hud_draw is the SOLE writer of the mission's termination
condition, and llm_tact_ui_order_buttons_minimap_tick calls llm_tact_group_issue_order four times
-- so a `hud`/`ui_` wall would delete the excursion's exit trigger and its minimap order buttons.
In the other direction llm_gfx_blit_sprite_rle, gfx_TransformBankData and llm_tlo_shade_table_build
_tact carry no tactical prefix at all and are walls.
TWO PROVENANCES, and the difference is deliberately visible in `settled_by`:
body-read                 -- a reviewer read the decompile AND the disassembly and traced a
consumer. Only `high` confidence verdicts became walls; every
`medium`, `low` or UNCERTAIN verdict was KEPT AS A MEMBER, which is
how the one direct contradiction in the fan-out resolved itself:
llm_tact_vision_cone_setup (WALL, medium) and
llm_tact_fov_probe_far_cell_and_door_state (MEMBER, high) write the
same five _G_LLM_TACT_FOV_* globals, so the pair stays in.
write-set enumeration     -- WEAKER. The whole measured global write set is renderer scratch and
the function is a blitter, a glyph drawer or the view-metrics
allocator. NOT a body read, so it does not see a write through a
pointer parameter -- which for these is the framebuffer, and is the
reason the weaker evidence is accepted here and nowhere else.
TACT1 owns re-examining any of these. Deleting an entry widens the domain, which is always safe;
adding one narrows it and needs a body read.

gfx_TransformBankData.why: Body only walks RLE run headers in bank_data and repacks each 16-bit pixel word (uVar2&0x1f)+((uVar2&0xffc0)>>1) back into bank_data -- a 5-5-5->5-6-5 style RGB565 recolor of a decoded sprite-bank image, guarded by `if (G_COLOR_FORMAT != RGB565) return`. docs/gfx-sprites.md corroborates it as an inline pixel-format conversion applied to loaded graphics banks.
